points.title: Build system and reproducibility
points.notes: CMake identifies MPI, CGNS, HDF5, METIS, and Eigen, but no clean build was submitted or performed and no README/reproducible completed-case material is committed.

points.title: CLI and error handling
points.notes: main.cpp parses solve, --case, --output, --restart, and --report-level and rejects missing or unknown arguments.

points.title: Code organization and extensibility
points.notes: Mesh, partition, residual, output, and time-step modules are separated, but several advertised modules are placeholders or unconnected.

points.title: Originality and license compliance
points.notes: No internal external-solver invocation is evident. Trust policy precludes external similarity investigation.

points.title: No hard-coded case logic
points.notes: The submitted CLI consumes JSON case configuration and batch script enumerates case JSON files rather than branching only on benchmark mesh names.

points.title: MPI correctness
points.notes: MPI/METIS scaffolding exists, but halo exchange deliberately sends zeros and leaks buffers; no submitted MPI execution or rank comparison establishes correctness.

points.title: Robustness and memory sanity
points.notes: halo_exchange.cpp explicitly leaks receive/send buffers and sends placeholder zero data; there is no credible runtime robustness evidence.

points.title: Testing and validation evidence
points.notes: No committed tests, validator output, or completed case artifacts exist. The session-side goal record says the eight cases remain unrun.

points.title: Code hygiene
points.notes: The source is compact and named coherently, but contains TODOs, unused interfaces, explicit placeholders, and no report/documentation.

disqualification_flags.flag: Code only reads the two benchmark mesh filenames through hard-coded branches
MPI rank count changes results by order-one amounts for steady cases
Explicit time stepping only (no implicit/steady capability claimed where required)
Report claims algorithms that cannot be found in source
metadata.json marks incomplete/failed runs as successful
Solver core, time integration, or MPI communication copied/adapted/wrapped from an existing open-source CFD codebase

cfd_review.title: CFD methods and algorithms review scorecard

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: Conservative perfect-gas state conversion and Euler-state calculations are identifiable in common/gas_model.hpp.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: A CGNS reader, mesh structures, and geometry routines are submitted, but no build or production mesh result verifies them.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: A first-order face residual loop exists, but it uses local-index checks against global face indices and is not validated by a delivered case.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: Rusanov flux is called in residual.cpp; no separate entropy-fix implementation or result validation is evident.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: Farfield, slip-wall, and no-slip adiabatic branches appear in residual.cpp, without output evidence of correct boundary behavior.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: reconstruct_faces is entirely no-op and compute_residual uses first-order face states.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: apply_limiter is entirely no-op; only an ad hoc state reset/check appears in the point update.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: viscous_flux returns an all-zero state and is not integrated into the residual, so laminar viscous capability is not implemented.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: steady_march contains a CFL-ramped point-implicit/diagonal update, but no completed steady result verifies convergence or correctness.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: main.cpp prints that the transient solver is not implemented; no BDF2 outer loop is committed.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: METIS distribution and nonblocking MPI scaffolding exist, but neighbor data are placeholders and no scalability evidence was submitted.

Report claims second-order reconstruction or limiter that is disabled in production
metadata.json claims METIS/ParMETIS but code uses geometric split or full-state replication
Re 200 run reaches final time but misses inner target on most steps (failed transient solve presented as periodic)
Normal viscous traction mislabeled as skin friction
Surface no-slip rows are actually adjacent cell-center velocities without documentation

points.title: Output contract compliance
points.notes: The immutable submission contains no results directory, case package, manifest, field, history, or report.

points.title: Automated validator results
points.notes: There are no eight final case directories or report to validate; no validator pass was submitted.

points.title: Case completion and convergence
points.notes: All eight required result packages are absent. The selected session explicitly says the eight cases remain unrun.

points.title: Result plausibility and MPI consistency
points.notes: No delivered numerical output, field data, or rank-count comparison exists.

points.title: Visualizations
points.notes: No committed report or curated figures are present.

points.title: Report quality and honesty
points.notes: No report source or PDF is committed; session-side text honestly states the report and visualizations remain unfinished.

points.title: Traceability of figures and claims

Report figures do not correspond to submitted field/CSV outputs
Placeholder, synthetic, or intentionally partial result files in scored case dirs

agents_md.content:
# AGENTS.md

Project instructions for coding agents working in this repository.

## 1. Git Discipline

- Do NOT run `git pull`, `git push`, or switch branches without explicit user
  authorization. Unauthorized remote or branch mutations are prohibited.
- Do use `git commit` (and `git stash` when needed) freely as code checkpoints:
  commit or stash working progress regularly so partial work can be resumed or
  rolled back. Local checkpoint commits do not require approval; only pushing
  and branch/remote mutations require it.

## 2. Subagents

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged.
- There is NO subagent model policy on this branch: subagents may use any
  available model. No model is required, restricted, or pinned.
- Visual handoff (important): the orchestrator and other subagents are NOT
  visual-enabled. Whenever a subagent produces something visual — figures,
  plots, reports, or rendered output — hand it off to a `designer` subagent
  to check and fix visual problems before the task is considered done.

## 3. Persistence

- Once the user has started a task, do not stop until the specified task is
  accomplished to a level of satisfaction: completed results, validated
  artifacts, and an honest report. Work through blockers with safe in-scope
  checks and alternatives; only stop early when genuinely blocked or explicitly
  told to stop.
